title: News: Downtown Squamish loses its only grocery store
context: You will hear a local radio news report about a grocery store closing in Squamish.

segments.speaker: News reader
segments.text: Shoppers in downtown Squamish are bracing for life without a grocery store. Cleveland Fresh Market, which has anchored the corner of Cleveland Avenue and Victoria Street for nearly thirty years, will close its doors on January thirty-first after its owners failed to reach a deal on a new lease.

segments.speaker: News reader
segments.text: The building's owner, Tantalus Holdings, plans to redevelop the site into a six-storey building with rental apartments upstairs and shops on the ground floor. The company says a grocer would be welcome back once construction wraps up, but it couldn't say when that might be, or whether rents would be within reach for an independent store.

segments.speaker: News reader
segments.text: For many downtown residents, the closure is more than an inconvenience. Ivana Kostić, who runs a seniors' walking group, says plenty of her members don't own cars, and the nearest supermarket is a forty-minute walk along the highway. She says the redevelopment is being sold as progress, but for people without a vehicle it amounts to two steps back.

segments.speaker: News reader
segments.text: Some residents aren't waiting for someone else to fix it. A group calling itself the Howe Sound Food Co-op has signed up more than four hundred households, each pledging two hundred dollars toward a member-owned store. Organizer Benoit Tremblay admits that's a far cry from the roughly one point five million dollars they'll need, but says the response proves the demand is there.

segments.speaker: News reader
segments.text: The district says it's exploring a free weekly shuttle to the highway shopping centres, starting in February.

questions.prompt: Why is Cleveland Fresh Market closing?

options.text: Its owners have decided to retire.
options.whyVi: Bài không nói chủ cửa hàng nghỉ hưu.

options.text: It could not agree on terms to stay in the building.
options.whyVi: Đúng: 'failed to reach a deal on a new lease' = không thỏa thuận được hợp đồng thuê mới.

options.text: Its sales fell after a supermarket opened nearby.
options.whyVi: Bài chỉ nói siêu thị gần nhất cách 40 phút đi bộ, không nói doanh số giảm.

options.text: The site will be turned into apartments with no shops.
options.whyVi: Chỉ đúng một phần: tòa nhà mới có căn hộ nhưng tầng trệt vẫn có cửa hàng.

questions.evidence: after its owners failed to reach a deal on a new lease
questions.explanationVi: 'failed to reach a deal on a new lease' được diễn đạt lại thành 'could not agree on terms to stay in the building'.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about a grocery store returning to the site?

options.text: A grocer has already agreed to move into the new building.
options.whyVi: Ngược lại: công ty chỉ nói 'would be welcome back', chưa có ai ký.

options.text: Tantalus Holdings will not rent space to grocery stores.
options.whyVi: Ngược lại: công ty nói sẽ chào đón cửa hàng tạp hóa quay lại.

options.text: The new building will be ready within a year.
options.whyVi: Công ty 'couldn't say when' – không nói thời gian.

options.text: It is far from certain that an independent shop could afford to come back.
options.whyVi: Đúng: công ty không chắc tiền thuê có 'within reach' (trong khả năng) của cửa hàng độc lập.

questions.evidence: whether rents would be within reach for an independent store
questions.explanationVi: Câu suy luận: lời nói tích cực 'welcome back' đi kèm hai điều không chắc (thời điểm, giá thuê). 'within reach' = có thể chi trả được. Đáp án D là suy luận hợp lý duy nhất.

questions.prompt: What is Ivana Kostić's view of the redevelopment?

options.text: It is presented as an improvement but would actually leave some residents worse off.
options.whyVi: Đúng: 'being sold as progress' nhưng với người không có xe thì 'two steps back' (thụt lùi).

options.text: She opposes building new rental housing downtown.
options.whyVi: Quá rộng: bà không phản đối nhà cho thuê, chỉ lo về việc mất cửa hàng tạp hóa.

options.text: A long walk to the supermarket is good exercise for her group.
options.whyVi: Bài có 'walking group' và 'forty-minute walk' nhưng bà xem đó là khó khăn.

options.text: She believes the project is real progress for the town.
options.whyVi: Ngược lại: 'being sold as progress' cho thấy bà hoài nghi lời quảng bá này.

questions.evidence: the redevelopment is being sold as progress, but for people without a vehicle it amounts to two steps back
questions.explanationVi: Thái độ ngầm: 'being sold as' = được quảng bá là (nhưng chưa chắc đúng). 'two steps back' = thụt lùi. Đáp án A diễn đạt lại thành 'presented as an improvement... worse off'.

questions.prompt: What does Benoit Tremblay mean when he talks about the money pledged?

options.text: The co-op has nearly reached its fundraising goal.
options.whyVi: Ngược lại: 'a far cry from' = còn rất xa.

options.text: The co-op has raised about two hundred thousand dollars.
options.whyVi: Sai: 400 hộ x 200 đô = khoảng 80.000 đô, và 200 là số tiền mỗi hộ.

options.text: The amount promised so far falls well short of what is required.
options.whyVi: Đúng: số tiền cam kết còn cách rất xa 1,5 triệu đô cần có.

options.text: The co-op will have to borrow one point five million dollars.
options.whyVi: Bài có con số 1,5 triệu nhưng đó là tổng chi phí cần, không nói phải vay.

questions.evidence: admits that's a far cry from the roughly one point five million dollars they'll need
questions.explanationVi: Thành ngữ 'a far cry from' = khác xa, còn rất xa so với. Đáp án C diễn đạt lại thành 'falls well short of'. Ông vẫn lạc quan vì 'the demand is there'.

questions.prompt: What does the report say about the shuttle?

options.text: It has already started running every day.
options.whyVi: Sai: mới đang được xem xét ('exploring'), dự kiến hằng tuần, bắt đầu tháng 2.

options.text: It is being considered as a weekly service at no cost to riders.
options.whyVi: Đúng: 'exploring a free weekly shuttle' = đang cân nhắc xe đưa đón miễn phí hằng tuần.

options.text: It will take residents to the new co-op store.
options.whyVi: Xe đưa đón đi tới các trung tâm mua sắm trên đường cao tốc, không phải cửa hàng co-op.

options.text: It will be paid for by Tantalus Holdings.
options.whyVi: Bài nói quận (the district) đang xem xét, không nhắc ai trả tiền.

questions.evidence: The district says it's exploring a free weekly shuttle to the highway shopping centres
questions.explanationVi: 'exploring' = đang xem xét, chưa chắc chắn ('being considered'); 'free' = 'at no cost'. Lựa chọn A bẫy vì bỏ qua từ 'exploring'.

vocabulary.definition: be the most important or central part of a place
vocabulary.example: The market has anchored the corner for thirty years.

vocabulary.definition: a legal agreement to rent a property
vocabulary.example: The owners could not agree on a new lease.
A grocer is welcome back once construction wraps up.
Rents may not be within reach for a small store.

vocabulary.definition: be presented to people as something positive
vocabulary.example: The project is being sold as progress.

vocabulary.definition: be the same as, in effect
vocabulary.example: For people without cars, it amounts to two steps back.

vocabulary.definition: very different from; much less than
vocabulary.example: The pledges are a far cry from the total they need.

vocabulary.definition: promise to give money or support
vocabulary.example: Each household pledged two hundred dollars.

vocabulary.definition: a vehicle that makes regular short trips between two places
vocabulary.example: A free shuttle may run to the shopping centres.

review.notes: Solved all 5 independently; keys match (BDACB); pledge maths (400 x $200 = $80,000 vs $1.5M) supports Q4. Renamed the developer from "Stawamus Holdings" (a Squamish Nation place name) to the fictional Tantalus Holdings.
